text_fidelity_a:
Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L I love this backpack! I commute by bike, and I wear those ridiculous spandex biking togs to keep cool whilst riding and not get my work clothes sweaty. Rather than packing a change of clothes every day, I take a week's worth of clothes in on Mondays. I like having the clothes in a backpack to I can easily take them to the restroom in the mornings to change, and keep the rest of them out of sight during the day. I was using a regular backpack, but that added weight, which is not great for biking, and it added bulk, meaning it was hard to fit everything in my pannier - I had to really stuff it in there and struggle a bit to fasten down the pannier's straps.

I bought this backpack in the hopes it would contain my clothes without excess weight or bulk. It's perfect! I have the 33L (largest) size, and it easily holds: 1 pair of (large) jeans, 5 shirts, 5 pairs of underwear, a couple of bras, a few pairs of socks, a microfiber washcloth and a small pack towel, with a bit of room to spare. It weighs virtually nothing, and adds almost no bulk, so now a week's worth of clothes fits easily in my pannier and doesn't weigh my bike down any more than absolutely necessary.

Since I have it at work anyway, I've used it to transport my laptop and other items, and it's plenty strong enough, and has enough useful pockets, to be an everyday backpack. My only small complaint would be that it lacks any structure. But that is, of course, by design, as it's meant to be folded up into a small package when not in use. But I never fold it up because I use it almost every day.

This was a great purchase. Very good value, high quality product, perfect for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle My experience with Kryptonite goes back to the period when one of their their original locks was found to be easily opened with a ballpoint pen. I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

One final note - Although I am sure no one else at Amazon would make this foolish mistake, when we left our B&B to head home from our last vacation I locked up the bikes and then left my cord with the keys to both locks draped over one of the handle bars while I checked the pressure on our car tires for the trip home. Of course I forgot about the keys and did not notice they were missing until we got home and tried to take our bikes off the rack. Luckily I was able to go into our house and get the spare keys that came with the locks. When I ordered replacements from Kryptonite they sent me new keys for both locks at no charge. Kryptonite provides excellent locks and they also provide excellent customer service!
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle

text_fidelity_a: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed I quite love this blade.. I bought the coated version to leave in my car as a utility knife, but very quickly it found its way into my pockets.. There are a few issues with this knife:  I had to immediately borrow a star key tool to change the clip over to the tang.. I don't really care if it carries tip up or down (comes tip down) but the clip is a bit large on this knife and just in the way, particularly for a knife with such great ergonomics.  The coating on the blade is also not the best.. Also mine had a few little imperfections throughout the blade- just a little pitting here and there.  Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.
text_fidelity_b: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed

text_fidelity_a: Katadyn Vario Water Filter, Dual Technology Microfilter for Personal or Small Group Camping, Backpacking or Emergency Preparedness I purchased this to take dry camping in the wilderness in Idaho. We two-party camping in off-road travel trailers next to a nice stream for a month and a half. To preserve our onboard water supply we filtered and filled 5 one-gallon water jugs for drinking water. After approximately 10 gallons I had to clean the ceramic filter with the included pad to keep it pumping easily. That operation is straightforward and simple. It takes just a few minutes to clean. I like that the pump is bidirectional....meaning, it pumps water while pushing in the handle and raising the handle. The final product was great-tasting drinking water. These streams are famous for having giardia but we had no problems at all. This pump likely prolonged our stay in the wilderness by weeks.  This was a fantastic and smart purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine We took delivery three weeks ago. Relatively easy to set up, but be aware that the seat likes to slide to the end of the stops. Now that we are used to it, my wife and I use it every day, sometimes multiple times a day. We don't put it away, just leave it in place next to the wall, facing the TV.
My main issue is that it, like all the other rowers I've seen, sits too low for someone who (like me) is 76 and 250lbs, with bad knees. At first, I'd either fall the last three inches, hopefully onto the seat, or need some sort of support to get on and off. I solved that problem by wrapping an old belt around the body (see pic), which I could use as a grab bar to lower myself on and lift myself off. If Sunny would put a grab handle on the front, that would be a big help, and save on belts.
A secondary issue is the LCD display. Others have complained that it's not bright enough. The real problem is that it's at the wrong angle. I repurposed a chunk of plastic foam packing to lift the bottom enough to make it clearly visible when seated. Sunny could duplicate that with a simple folding frame.
I should also note that the labeling on the display is wrong. Label says: Time, Count, Total Count, Calories. Actual is: Time, Count, Calories, Total Count.
Finally, I note that almost all of the self-help videos on rowing emphasize managing your strokes per minute. The display doesn't show that. I'd be willing to give up both Total Count and Calories to get that in the display. After all, Total Count is only useful if you are the only person using the machine, and Calories are pretty much a meaningless guess without information like body weight.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine

text_fidelity_a:
TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641 I have gone back to a wheel gun for concealed carry because I can't afford the one time that I might need to use my defensive weapon and have it jam. I know, I know! The modern semi autos are basically fool proof and malfunctions only happen occasionally. And I know that even with a subcompact you can easily carry 8-10 rounds of whatever, but I learned a long time ago that the more moving parts in any machine/tool, the more potential problems can happen -- and usually at the worst possible time. (Thank you Mr. Murphy).

My new defensive carry is a Smith & Wesson Model 327 2" Performance Center that holds eight rounds of 38 Special/ 38 +P/357 Magnum. It is a rather large revolver made of scandium and has a large grip which fits my hand perfectly. I'm a big guy so it's really no problem to conceal and the 2" barrel should make it qualify (in court) as a defensive weapon should I have to use it. My backup is a Ruger LCR in 357, a light and tiny gun that is a devil to shoot full power loads in. Fortunately I'm a big fan of 44 magnums and am comfortable handling a lot of recoil. Why the Ruger LCR as backup? There's nothing like redundancy in personal defense. A second gun using the same ammo covers most of the bases.

The result is that I can carry two revolvers loaded with a total of 13 rounds -- equaling or surpassing any of the subcompact/compact autos -- that will both go "Bang" when needed. And, and this is a big "And", any family member or passerby will also be able to operate either one of them should I be in trouble/incapacitated. All you have to do is pull the trigger. The alternative is a semi auto that might pose operating difficulty to whomever tries to be of assistance. There won't be enough time to lecture anyone on the operating mechanics of a semi auto.

So I picked up two QuickStrips and this pouch. Putting in two of the strips, one facing up and one facing down, creates a relatively slim package holding an additional ten rounds -- on top of the thirteen already loaded in the two revolvers. The total of 23 rounds should be enough for 99% of the potential situations encountered in most areas. I try to keep myself out of dangerous areas/predicaments (situational awareness), but if I have to enter one I will have a Glock 19 as my backup. A good man knows his limitations.
text_fidelity_b: TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641

text_fidelity_a: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras I have three bird feeders in my yard - they are all three very close to each other.  I have five different nectar feeders and three seed feeders as well as bird baths.  I set this camera up so I could see who all are coming in for food and water.  It's been fun seeing the hummingbirds hovering to sip the sugar water and the Chickadees and other small birds come for the seeds.  I have a traditional bird bath but watching with the trail camera, I found that the birds like my solar water "fountain" made from an automatic cat water fountain - I followed a video and used a small styrofoam ball with a hole through it and the tube from the water pump just a little over the top of the foam ball.  The hummingbirds love holding onto the foam ball and sipping water, even dunking their little heads in the bubbling water.  It's been fun watching them without disturbing them - that's why I love this camera.  The birds are used to it sitting there and don't even pay attention, all the while I get to see what they are doing.  So cool!
text_fidelity_b: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Cressi Pro Light, black, XS These are great fins, their thrust vector is excellent, they are easy to get on and off, the clips on the strap work well and are very heavy duty, all in all a very good fin.

I just have one problem with them and it's not such a problem that I'd go looking for a different fin. The heel strap tends to work down off my heel over time no matter how much I tighten it up, and you don't want it so tight that it pinches and gets uncomfortable over time as you wear it. This might be partly because I wear a 3mm neoprene wet sock with them. I do that because putting flippers on in sand without a wet sock (a sock made of wetsuit material) is asking for abrasions on your foot. The heel strap tends to pull the sock down and the whole thing eventually slips off the bottom of my heel. This is the first time I've used an open foot fin with socks, usually I use a full foot fin and this isn't an issue. Every so often I have to reach down and pull the heel strap up. It's not a deal killer, I'm not sorry I got this fin, it's a minor irritation that is most likely due to the way I use them.

That's the only problem I've had with these fins so I'm describing it to be honest and thorough about this item.
text_fidelity_b: Cressi Pro Light, black, XS

text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover Finally got a chance to take the bag out and put it though it’s paces. We don’t have any camping trips planned for now, but we put a towel and 10 lbs of weight and off we went. He’s 6 feet and skinny for reference. Took it for a thirty minute walk in 90 degrees F and 49% humidity. The pack felt good. The air gap was great, and kept him from overheating. He said the bag sat well and didn’t shift once secured. He is right handed and a lot like my other hiking backpacks, there is only a zipper pocket in the left waist band. This is because you don’t usually reach across to get something in your waist pocket on a hike. The right side is a non zip folded pocket. The rain cover stuffs in a Velcro pocket on the bottom and fits snugly over the entire pack. The large roomy main compartment fits everything I would need for a weekend hike, or a long day hike. Food, camp stove, change of clothing, single man tent, jacket and the large capacity reservoir. There is a hook to put the reservoir on so it doesn’t slip down as you empty the bladder. The bite valve is the standard camelback with shut off (this is important if you have ever been hiking and broken your bite valve and didn’t have time to dig out a spare until base camp.) this is Not a carry your laptop and tootle around town pack. This is a well made solid day/weekend hiker. Yes it would be nice to have a small inner zip pocket, but that’s what carabiners and dry sacks are for. It has a mesh two compartment pocket, and a larger pocket the whole bag length. Water reservoir has its own zippered compartment, and there is one center small zip pocket for quick access item like headlamp. Has a large adjustable mesh pocket on the outside that you can put a helmet, or ground roll. Can’t wait for camping to open up again, I may just steal this from my husband for scout campouts. Product free in exchange for an honest review.

text_fidelity_a:
ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones We were so looking forward to receiving this hammock - but when it arrived, our hopes and dreams were dashed to the ground like refuse thrown into a gutter! The hammock took longer than expected to arrive - but not to worry-- we patiently checked Amazon tracking on a daily basis to see when the refreshment of lying on a soft, sturdy hammock whilst sipping a cocktail - would arrive at our door. After waiting on the edge of our plastic lawn chairs for two weeks, the big day finally arrived! The hammock was delivered by our friendly Amazon courier and shouts of joy could be heart resounding through the halls of our home! Two of our sons ceremoniously carried the long hammock box into the house like a wealthy Roman patron being carried through the streets on a litter. The box was opened and said hammock was unrolled like a precious scroll. Visions of hours spent snoozing under a canopy of trees danced in the heads of family members as they clamored to put this 'Object of 'Liesure and Rest' onto the stand that had carried our old, canvas, LL BEAN hammock. After 14 years of service, that good sanctuary had finally rotted away. (Actually, I wasn't home for this part, but I'm sure this is how it went.)

Our faithful and strong sons set the hammock up beneath towering Tulip Populars, wafting in the refreshing breeze and waited for me to come home hoping to unveil a pleasant surprise for the beloved mother. I arrived home, hot, sweaty and tired from a long day of horseback riding with my faithful steed. A persistent headache was pounding in my brain from hours of tracking desperados through the forests. (Ok, I was actually trying to catch up to my friends who had galloped away rather prematurely.) Anyway, as I slogged through the house, wilted and exhausted, my god-like son winked at me whilst ushering me through the back door to the paradise that awaited in the back yard.

THERE IT WAS! THE HAMMOCK for which I had been longing! I sat down on the side and stretched my battered frame onto the hammock like Cleopatra reclining under a gold-embroidered canopy dressed as Aphrodite, (but wearing riding boots and half-chaps).....only to discover that the hammock of my dreams was an imposter!!!! THIS WAS NO SOFT BED OF ROSES TO LIE ON! NO! IT FELT LIKE BAD CARPET ON THE WALLS OF A CHEAP MOTEL! I stifled my revulsion and tried to get comfortable but it was no use. The fabric wasn't fabric at all - it felt like plastic water bottles woven into a nightmarish tapestry by well-intentioned environmentalists! I leapt from this bed of vipers disgusted and disappointed. My family pleaded with me to give it another chance, saying "It's not so bad, we like it!" "Philistines!!!!" I retorted! " THIS. WILL. NOT. DO!" whilst gnashing my teeth to the best of my ability. To which they shrugged and got the box out of the trash so we could return it.

Postscript - If you want a comfy hammock made out of sunbrella fabric, you have to spend about $250 these days. I found one on Wayfair and now we are anxiously awaiting that one to be delivered. Cheers! :)
text_fidelity_b: ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones

SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap The LED light is bright enough to help you get your key into a lock, but it'll only dimly light your path. The alarm sound is not very loud--not as loud as a car alarm or a whistle or a smoke alarm. It doesn't help that the speaker is on the back, where your hand naturally covers it to some degree. It makes a weird noise that didn't even grab the attention of a man sitting 70 feet away because it sounded like just another mechanical noise rather than an alarm. The stun gun made more noise! Personally, I'd hoped the light and the alarm noise would warn most potential attackers away, but I doubt they'll be much help. Since the light and the sound aren't as impressive as they advertised, I do wonder if the stun gun will be very effective, but I'm not going to test it out on anyone! They say it's most effective on certain parts of the body, so you have to be close and even aim somewhat, not just touch the current to some body part.

Anyway, you get a USB charging cord and have to charge the stun gun 12 hours before the first use and 4-5 hours each week. Though the green (full charge indicator) light turns on after only a couple hours, they stress the length of time spent on charging more than the indicator light. There is an on/off switch than must be turned on before the alarm sound or the stun gun button will work. The light button will work at all times. The buttons are easy to use, though the labeling on them is not easy to read (especially at night). The light stays on until pressed off, which means it can be turned on if something presses the button when in your purse. This could run the battery down so it's not effective when needed. Some way to check how much charge is left would have been useful. I've never seen or used a stun gun before, but this seemed more hype than useful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap

Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. However, this little unit worked incredibly well.

It charges quickly via USB Micro (120 minutes to full charge / with 30 inflates per charge), has all of the accessories needed to get going (USB cable, air needles, attachment hose, etc..), has pre-set modes for a football, a soccer ball, a basketball, etc.. And is super compact & lightweight (6.29" x 1.4" & weighing only 6.5oz).

I haven't tried, but don't see why you couldn't even inflate a bicycle tire with this unit as well. However, I probably wouldn't try with anything larger like a car or truck tire out of concern of damaging the pump.

There is an auto-shut off option (IE: when you use a ball preset the pump will turn off when it dispenses the appropriate amount of air for the selected ball), however, there is no pressure gauge. So, if you don't use the preset, then you have to go by feel (or have an air gauge on hand).

As far as my experiment, I didn't even use the presets. Just popped in the needle into my slam ball & turned on the pump. It inflated (my very deflated) slam ball in a matter of seconds. A success!

If you're constantly using a foot pump or bike pump to inflate your sports equipment, bike tires, etc.., then seriously consider this portable pump instead. Makes this process super easy. There's even an attachment that looks like it's to be used for blowing up balloons! Very cool!

text_fidelity_a:
Triple-Insulated Stainless-Steel Water Bottle Flip-Top Lid - (20 oz) Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Wide Mouth and Leakproof - Canteen Water Bottle Great for Office, School, Biking Etc. My water bottle should:
1. Open easily with one hand
2. Keep the water cold
3. Be tough
4. Be easy to drink from
5. Be easy to clean.
6. (Extra credit) Be really easy to carry. Or not be bad at it.

I don't want to suck the water; I prefer to pour it into my mouth. So a tiny hole or straw is a no-go.

I had an Aladdin that was all that, but the spring eventually broke. Can't open one-handed anymore.

I bought a variety of water bottles to try out. This is my favorite. It's all of the above, with one caveat and one addition.

It opens easily, as long as there's no vacuum lock (i.e. you didn't put ice in and close it, resulting in the air inside cooling and forming suction.) The thermos is great. It's made of metal and heavy plastic.

IF you move the handle (the white ring) back BEFORE you open the bottle, it's easy to drink from. Otherwise the spout doesn't really come out far enough to get it close to your mouth. But that's easy to do.

Fully dishwasher safe. And very easy to carry, especially with that large handle/carry ring. Which is a solid loop. An example of this done badly is many of the UnderArmor bottles, which have a split ring for carrying that you really can't carry with a finger when full because the prongs of the split point in and dig into your finger.

The Extra Credit: There's a screen to prevent random ice bits from going into your mouth. It's removable, but I love this thing. I like my sports-water cold, but don't want to chew on ice during exercise.
text_fidelity_b: Triple-Insulated Stainless-Steel Water Bottle Flip-Top Lid - (20 oz) Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Wide Mouth and Leakproof - Canteen Water Bottle Great for Office, School, Biking Etc.

text_fidelity_a:
MSR SweetWater Microfilter While gravity filters have become the most popular backpacking water filters because no pumping is required, pump filters are still essential in situations where you only have access to shallow water sources. And that's why I went with the MSR SweetWater for a 5 night backpacking trip in the Grand Canyon backcountry — all of the water sources were shallow streams.

Pump filters aren't fast, but only having to filter 3 to 4 liters a day for myself really wasn't much of a chore. If this was the only filter for a group of people, then I'd say figure out a way to use a gravity filter.

I never got sick, so I suppose that's some kind of sign that the filter worked. It didn't, though, fully remove odors from the water. The water at one of the places I filled up had a slight swampy smell to it that was still there after I filtered.

The Nalgene attachment that it comes with is quite useful. The overall weight and size are also good for backpacking.

Note: You absolutely have to always use the prefilter. If you don't, tiny pebbles will get sucked in and obstruct the plunger. I don't get why MSR makes the prefilter an attachment rather than permanently part of the inhouse. Well, actually I guess they do that so you can replace the hose without also replacing the prefilter, but they're just inviting people to use the filter without the prefilter. Speaking from experience, if a pebble does get stuck in there it's not to hard to get it out. But always bring a backup filter.
text_fidelity_b: MSR SweetWater Microfilter

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)
text_fidelity_b: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag

Although it doesn't get in the way of my shifting or brake cables, I can see a configuration where it would. A more adaptable mounting mechanism may be in order to handle a larger number of bike variants.

My initial response was that I wish it had more light modes but after using it on the streets and trails round Boston I've found 2 that I switch between and I'm happy. The "Steady Pulse" works well for traffic notification. I've watched cars very specifically react to the light at a good distance even though I'm angling it down to not blind too many people. I can also see it flicker on reflective paint on signs so I know it's got good distance. I also use the low setting for dark bike baths so I don't blind oncoming bikers/runners. I can also easily angle it to one side or the other as well to get it out of people's faces.

Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps… For under 100 bucks shipped you get everything you need to get out on the water minus life vests. The skeg has been improved as it now has a new locking mechanism and silhouette. The 86" paddles are well made for the price, nicely curved, have an adjustable paddle angle and float (as we found out accidentally) so paddle leashes are recommend. The boat is stable when inflated properly using the pressure gauge "measuring strip" and did not rock too bad when standing up in the aft position with an adult seated up front. The boat has a drain plug in the stern which has to be closed as mine was shipped in the open position. The 30 gauge PVC (Vinyl) has a nylon like backing and appears to be rugged enough for large lakes and mild moving waters. Not sure I would personally use this on class III+ water but some reviewer's have reported their own success stories. It tracks well on flat water with the skeg and okay with a peaceful river current without. Seats are more comfortable than I originally imagined when purchasing. Watch out for over inflation as we pumped her up at 64° and by the afternoon the temp had increased to 74° which caused the inflation gauge to read 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) higher due to air expansion. Over all I am impressed for the cost of purchase. It comes with one 3"x3" self adhesive patch similar to "Tear-Aid type B" (looks like a square piece of yellow card stock) and two 2" clear patches that require you to use your own PVC cement. The pump tube can be stored inside the pump itself by unscrewing the end and coiling it around the pump shaft. It packs up into a Blackhawk tactical bag that I have as the Intex bag was uncomfortable to carry since it didn't have a shoulder strap. The boat is 22.2 lbs without the seats, 25.8 lbs with both seats not including other accessories. Takes about 10 minutes to setup with the included air pump or 5 minutes with the 12v Intex pump (which has deflate mode too!!!).

Things to remember include closing the drain plug and monitoring inflation to prevent over inflation related seam tears. If you know the temp will increase throughout the day by 5-10° i would recommend under inflating by 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) on the inflation gauge which is approximately 10 cm long when fully inflated.
text_fidelity_b: Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps…

text_fidelity_a:
Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue) I grabbed this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair with a thought towards our days at the beach. Sometimes we have chairs, sometimes just the towels, but I thought this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair might offer me a nice, supportive place to sit. My wife tends to lay out for sun, but I like watching the water and thinking... but I can get tired and start to hurt on the hard sand. This is smaller and easier to carry overall (I thought), so why not. In the end, I think I’m going to be correct in my assessment. We’re not getting back out there (yet), but the time is soon upon us for our beach days and I can’t wait.

The Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair is a cool idea - a stadium seat type set up: flips open, cushion, back support. I’ve tried one or two such seats and thought, eh. But we don’t do stadiums enough. We do, however, sit on the floor from time to time, go to the beach, mediate, and so forth. Hitting that “middle age” timeframe, my wife and I would love to have something more comfortable.

1. I gave it 5 stars because overall it feels like that’s right for comfort, ease of use, and so forth. I would consider a 4 star for the magnets that hold the seat to the frame. I’ve had the seat cushions pop off every time I’ve picked it up to carry/move, or take pictures. My wife has not as such luck, only having them fall a couple time. Closed they’d slide up coming off for me, so I’d be worried about loosing one or two or all three - though I’m sure one would notice that many.

2. The cushions are nice for comfort. It comes with three, with one having a strap on the back to hold it onto the other - so you can have a double seat cushion, which is a nice add on.

3. Seems to hold a good amount of weight. I’ve got some extra pounds on right now and it seems to handle me well. I’m taking it off, so hoping it won’t be there all summer as I plan to use it, but so far, so good.

4. The frame seems solid and like it’ll hold up. Again, it holds our weight (individually) and allows us to feel well supported. My wife has tried it more, sitting both cross legged and straight and feels like she can sit there for a good amount of time in both positions.

5. The seat cushions are good - not too thick (though thicker is always better), but not too thin. They were comfortable on both the back and seat.

6. This Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair comes with a strap that you can remove, attaching to the base of the frame allowing you to carry it over the shoulder. My wife did this and felt like both the strap was comfortable, while the chair was not too heavy. We both agree this is a solid, with a noticeable weight to it, but nothing most folks couldn’t handle (we think), finding the strap to be a good addition to aiding that. This is where you’ll want to be aware of the magnets not necessarily holding the seat in place - at least one popped off each time I tried, but only once for my wife. Because of how it sets when you are carrying on the strap - with the open side downward - it would allow the cushion to slip out onto the ground. I grabbed it before it did, but one needs to be aware, so as not to loose any. We talked about adding a strap of our own (sort of a bungie type thing) to hold the cushions in place. But that could be used for other things as well - we just don’t know what that is at this point.

7. Back support - we have only used it on the bed (that was not working too well as we’d fall over, but it was fun trying) and floor in the living room. But the back support was solid and let us feel comfortable. We both felt like it would be a nice support and keep us from hunching over and getting sore quickly.

In the end we are both impressed with this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair and plan to get some solid use out of it. I think this will be one item where time will tell - does it hold up, does it allow for longer periods of sitting, does it take different surfaces (beach, floor, grass, etc)? We’re happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight Everyone knows the first rule: You get what you pay for. In this case though I think that you get more than what you expect. My experience so far is that this scope functions flawlessly. That has proven how well the Chinese can reverse engineer some products and manufacture them to relatively high standards. I would certainly be afraid to drop it but it is screwed together very well.

The second rule I abide by is: The more complicated the product, the more things that can go wrong with it. And this particular product has a lot of technical features. Think of it as a Swiss Army Knife but with battery powered components. It is actually designed quite well and looks good properly mounted but I doubt that it would continuously handle the recoil from a large caliber rifle or shotgun. However there is a 30 day "Money Back Satisfaction Guarantee" and a 12-month warranty if it goes bad.

The third rule that I usually follow is to buy at least one model higher (in price and quality) when I determine what I might need. In this case though it makes more sense to not get a more complicated scope/laser combo. Shooting/hunting is complicated enough depending on how your weapon functions, the conditions you're shooting under, and your ability to master the situation to end up successful. Typically the more things that can get in your way during a shooting situation can limit your results dramatically. So I always try to keep it simple.

This is a fun product however -- just make sure that you use it a lot during the initial 12 months. By then you will know what functions are most important to you, which weapon pairs with it the best (for you), and how dependable it is. Perhaps you only need a fixed blade knife instead of that Swiss Army Knife.
text_fidelity_b: UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight

VENZO Compatible with Shimano SPD Mountain Bike CNC Cr-Mo Die-Cast Aluminum Sealed Pedals with Cleats - Dual Platform Clipless Pedals for Mountain Bike Shoes - Easy Clip in & Out I'm not really much of a bike rider, but lately I've been going on some longer trips (about 20 miles once a week or so) and decided that it might be worth my while to invest in some clip in pedals. After reading about the two main types of clipless systems, I decided the SPD-style pedals would better fit my bill and budget, and desire to stay around $100 together with shoes. Installation was a breeze, once I purchased an additional wrench to get my unexpectedly heavy old regular rectangle pedals off, and these Venzo brand pedals slipped right into place.

I haven't had any issues with the tension of the clipping mechanism after three solid rides so far, though I did have a bolt fall out of my shoe causing the shoe to get stuck clipped into the pedal -- I releasing the tension all the way got the shoe out but the small metal piece which the tension screw screws into is rather difficult to get back into position if it happens to fall out.

The included cleats fit nicely on the shoes I bought and other than some embarrassing falls and general awkwardness getting in/out of the pedals, I haven't had any issues with these pedals. If you are a beginning cyclist like myself looking for an affordable entry to clipless pedal systems, these fit the bill well. I also have taken some shorter trips with regular non clip-in shoes with these and they are acceptably fine.
text_fidelity_b: VENZO Compatible with Shimano SPD Mountain Bike CNC Cr-Mo Die-Cast Aluminum Sealed Pedals with Cleats - Dual Platform Clipless Pedals for Mountain Bike Shoes - Easy Clip in & Out

text_fidelity_a:
Vivi Electric Bike for Adults 26" Ebike, 500W Folding Electric Bike, 20MPH Adult Electric Bicycles with Removable 48V Battery, Up to 50Miles Range, Shimano 21 Speed, Dual Shock Absorber At first, the power and quickness of the electrical assist surprised me, but I got comfortable in no time. I hate to admit it, but I find myself using the electric mode (which requires no pedaling) more and more everyday. It is much like a scooter and very fun. Overall the bike handles like a cruiser and pedals with ease given 7 gear options. The shifter works well and does not get hung up too often. 

The bike is heavier with the battery but it is not that noticeable. The battery can also be removed when you know you won't be using it, or when you're charging it. It is GREAT that this has disc brakes to slow down the power of an electric bike. I kept track and for over one week, 1 hr/day, ~15 miles using assist and electric only mode, the battery indicator shows half life. It folds down to a more compact size, which is so useful if you want to transport it in your car, or fold it up for storage.  We got this initially for grandma to be able to keep up with the kids.  It turned out to be too high for her legs at the lowest setting (she's 5'1"").  My wife (5'4"") has no issues and loves using this bike with the kids. Overall, we never expected to be so won over by electric bikes; this is a great ride, and at a great price for what you're getting. There are other 'bells and whistles' included like a very loud alarm and front/back lights/accessories that add to overall biking safety and comfort.

Unboxing the bicycle was easy and the package included all the tools needed for assembly. It took about 30 minutes to put together (handle bars, seat, front wheel, fenders, pedals, air pumped into tires). There was no instruction manual in the box and the QR code led to nowhere, but I was able to find how-to videos on other similar models.  I also later found that they emailed me some tips, which were helpful.  Speaking of the seller, we contacted them because of an issue with the battery and they resolved it quickly; we were happy to see that they offered good customer service. Would be a perfect commuter's bike.
text_fidelity_b: Vivi Electric Bike for Adults 26" Ebike, 500W Folding Electric Bike, 20MPH Adult Electric Bicycles with Removable 48V Battery, Up to 50Miles Range, Shimano 21 Speed, Dual Shock Absorber

How I got it considering the cardboard box was completely sticking out of the open-ended mailer is beyond me, but again, I am thankful this bottle came to me intact.  My only real complaint about this bottle is the size of the opening.  I say this because I carry a water bottle to work every day and I use ice cubes in my regular bottle to keep the water cold for a long time.  My traditional bottle has a wide-mouth opening and I have an ice cube tray that makes nearly 2 inch square ice cubes - big ice cubes that melt a bit more slowly that regular-sized cubes.  This water bottle has a fairly narrow opening so I might be able to fit smaller ice cubes in it which is fine, but I did like having the big ice cubes in my water bottle because they do melt more slowly, keeping the water cold longer.  So, back to the bottle itself - I like that you have a choice between the regular screw cap and the one that has a flip-open straw opening.  This one is a bit taller than my other water bottle, but not quite as big around so I'm pretty sure that, internally, they both hold the same amount of liquid.
